title: Astra Blew Me Away
author: Shamrock21191
selftext: I have been working on making a couple of video games with Sol being the main coder and me being art and director and some friends helping where they could. I had a lot of good progress with Sol mostly. The biggest issues were creature designs looking nowhere close to my drawings or concept art in 3D. I decided to have Astra remake my creatures in 3d following prompts from Sol and making the same creatures from scratch and it made them very close on the first try and better in every single way. Then for shits and giggles I had it redesign my starting town from scratch using only what was discussed in the game Bible. Just for a test... until it made such an improved town that it is now my new starting town (with a few changes). I couldn't believe it. I dont know if I am allowed to promote so I won't share anything. I just thought it was cool as hell.

replies.author: EchoingAngel
replies.body: As a power AI user for game dev, I felt like this one had more "soul". The new one probably could be refined to this level, but it feels generic (which basically most "one shots" will be)

replies.author: Shamrock21191
replies.body: Oh yeah, I was just talking about the overall land being not flat and similar in the new one. This was just the very first look at it. I am refining it and adding the soul back into it by adding my own touches and design things into it. Also dynamic weather and lighting and day night cycles. The first town had all that in that picture the new one is still implementing those systems in, so as of right now it looks more generic.

replies.author: EchoingAngel
replies.body: Is that in an Astra accessible repo? I have it dig through my git repo when swapping to new versions and making sure it tries applying all the specifics that used to exist. Generally it isn't perfect, but it's a nice jumpstart

replies.author: Shamrock21191
replies.body: It is, everything is in there. We're doing it in stages though. Before I trust it completely lol.

comments.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
comments.body:
Can you teach me what ingame bible means? How did you get GPT to acknowledge those words?  
I learned about Vertical Slicing today and that was exciting. I have taken my development to the next level by slicing my program up and making tiny versions of the final copy.

Bible is like laws of physics for the world? It would help me if you used your own words and described what ingame bible meant to you.

replies.author: Shamrock21191
replies.body: Thats pretty close. It is just a fancy way of saying lore and rules to follow so that way we dont do anything wrong

comments.author: HealthPuzzleheaded
comments.body:
But I really dont get why you guys all try to use codex/claude to create the models, rigs e.t.c.
Why not use a dedicated tool there are cheap services and also good free  local alternatives to model, texture, rig at almost AAA Quality.

replies.author: whenItFits
replies.body: Why not list the ones your talking about?

replies.author: _HoundOfJustice
replies.body: Well there are none - at least not any that come anywhere close to AAA quality level and below that either. Not even paid ones get there.

replies.author: cxfoulke
replies.body:
Yeah my experience has been this... The higher fidelity you get, the more you see the flaws in the models and animations.  Also much harder to keep a consistent style. 

Also once you use higher quality models you need higher quality vfx and the pipelines for thoses are very underdeveloped.

Llm built models get the job done for prototype or low poly stuff.

replies.author: _HoundOfJustice
replies.body: Exactly. It works as a base mesh eventually but even there you have to be careful and it can be really nasty to fix those when you want to work on top of the mesh. I also never texture again when generating 3D meshes and for 3D printing i dont need those and neither do i need those for game development and assets i use for serious purposes except that i currently experiment with using AI meshes as base meshes to work on top of inside of Zbrush or 3ds Max. Texturing is always being done in Substance 3D.

replies.author: HealthPuzzleheaded
replies.body:
dont wanted it to sound like an ad. I use tripo P2.0.
some people suggest meshy but I think tripo has an edge because of the good topology while you need to run meshy models through a pipeline to make them game ready.

replies.author: pixelvspixel
replies.body: Yeah p2.0 is pretty impressive for generating quads. I haven’t found anything on par.

replies.author: TraditionalDeal9526
replies.body: Can also use BlenderMCP and connect Codex straight to it. It’s pretty good

replies.author: HealthPuzzleheaded
replies.body:
yea but why?
Use a dedicated ai model to create the thing you need. then use blendermcp to clean up the rough edges.

replies.author: Shamrock21191
replies.body: I tried doing that with 3 different AI services. Meshy, Tripo, and one other that the name is escaping me. While they looked good, they had lots of flaws and made rigging and animation so much harder. Its better to use them to create the static and then have Codex use it as a visual guide to create its own version that is easier to rig.

comments.author: EchoingAngel
comments.body: I had Astra redo my main UI background images to get away from Sol's AI sloppiness. It took 10 hours to get all 4 properly straightened out, but as the main "AI slop" visuals in the game, I think it was worth spending the time to reduce that feel. Once things get a point of people not knowing for sure (AI vs hand made), I think that's the sweet spot.

replies.author: Shamrock21191
replies.body: Yes I am spending hours making sure it doesnt feel like AI slop. From the few people ive had look at the current builds even anti AI people thought it was decent. Not GOOD but okay lol.
